title: Dream Feed closes this weekend so you only have a few more chances to...
transcript: You know that moment right before you wake up when you're still half in a dream and all you want to do is sink back into that dream that you're being forced out of? That is what it felt like watching dream Feed. Dream feed is a song cycle of sorts created by the hawtplates, which is Justin Hicks, Kenita Miller-Hicks and Jade Hicks. And it's like a live concept album of the idea of dream. Sort of like explaining a dream. Explaining dream feed is just hard to do, but I was engrossed from start to finish. Did I understand what was going on? Hardly. Did not matter. It very much felt to me like a Heather Christian show, similar to Terce and oratorio for living things. Just that being in a room surrounded by a community audience has these incredible vocalists and musicians are bathing you in the sound of their concept. I was engrossed from beginning to end and the sounds that they created in this incredibly intimate space, from their vocals and gorgeous three part harmonies to this giant wind chime sculpture that they had in the centre of the room. And each of these songs captured the feeling of a dream or trying to describe a dream or the dream like world that your mind takes you on as you sleep. They took us on a journey that I did not wanna wake up from. This is definitely not the kind of theatre If you want to think about the state of the world and how can we make the world a better place, this is very much the kind of theatre that is an experience. It's something that you go in with a group of strangers and feel something for 80 some odd minutes. It is like the spa equivalent of live theatre. It was relaxing and engaging and hauntingly beautiful and daringly intimate as they he sang these gorgeous melodies in your face. I am so glad that I got to experience this. And again if you are a fan of shows like terce and oratorio for living things, I cannot recommend this enough. Very much in the same vein as far as tickets go, this is only playing until February 1st. They do offer some unique show times. There's four PM shows, there's 8:30 shows and it is under 90 minutes and tickets are as cheap as $10 as part of their access program. So incredibly affordable. And I highly, highly highly recommend that if you're available in the next week that you try to catch this one. I really, really enjoyed it.
